Let’s reason through this step by step.  

1. The Treaty of Tordesillas (1494) divided newly discovered lands between Spain and Portugal along a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands.  
2. Portugal got lands to the east of the line; Spain got lands to the west.  
3. At this time, Portuguese explorers had already been exploring the African coast, seeking a sea route to India to bypass overland Muslim-controlled trade routes.  
4. In 1488, Bartolomeu Dias had already rounded the Cape of Good Hope, proving a sea route to the Indian Ocean was possible.  
5. Vasco da Gama would reach India in 1498, but by 1494 Portugal already knew the eastern route around Africa was viable.  
6. This explains why Portugal wanted the eastern side of the line — it secured their route to India and trade with Asia, not the New World (which was mostly west of the line).  

Option (D) fits because the Portuguese knew of the route to India via the Cape of Good Hope and wanted to secure their monopoly on that trade.  

Final answer: (D)
